full_judgment: 11. Plaintiff's case is that plaintiff Dabiruddin had been suffering from Typhoid and while he was senseless, the father of defendant nos.1-2 called a man and identified him as a doctor who took thumb impression of Dabiruddin on three sheets of papers. It is not the case of the plaintiff that Dabiruddin executed Heba-bil-ewaj deed on condition that the father of the defendant nos.1-2 would transfer 2(two) annas share inherited by their mother Fulijan Bibi from Daresh Khan in favour of Dabiruddin. Order 14 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides settlement of issues and determination of suit on issues of law or on issues agreed upon. It appears that the learned Munsif framed the issues as stated above and no issue has been framed regarding exchange of land as per pleadings of the defendants. The only point the appellate court below took for determination is "are the judgment and decree under appeal sustainable." The appellate court below did not frame any issue on the basis of the pleadings of the defendant nos.1 and 2 and without adverting the findings of the trial court arrived at a conclusion that the Heba-bil-ewaj was executed on a condition to exchange lands between the parties. In many of the decisions this court held that where appellate court failed to advert the reasoning's of the trial court and also did not reverse the findings of the trial court, the judgment of the appellate court is not sustainable in law. It is also held to hand down a judgment of reversal, the appellate court is required to consider the judgment and order of the trial court and then to reverse the findings of the trial court with sufficient reasons. A judgment reversing the decree of the trial court without adverting to the evidence on which the trial court relied is not a proper judgment of reversal and is liable to he set aside.
